critical_code_review_comments: Playwright's synthetic drag_and_drop did NOT trigger HTML5 native dragstart/drop on PipelinePage cards — this is a well-known Playwright limitation with HTML5 native DnD, NOT a product bug. The backend POST /pipeline/prospects/{id}/move is fully verified via pytest (200 + 400 + 404 + idempotent same-stage). For UI regression coverage going forward, consider either (a) switching to react-dnd-html5-backend (which Playwright handles better) OR (b) wrap each drop zone with an explicit invisible 'Move here' button accepting the same testid-tagged action — this makes the column-transition flow keyboard-accessible and testable simultaneously. Non-blocking.
PipelinePage.jsx is 844 lines — still readable but approaching the >700 split threshold; the prospect drawer is the natural extraction candidate.

TeamActivityWidget refresh interval (30s) is fine for now; once more clients onboard, consider a single shared interval at the portal page level + a context provider to avoid N timers when the widget remounts across tab switches.
GET /pipeline/prospects/{id}/ai-suggestion fallback path is deterministic and stage-aware — confirmed via test_ai_suggestion. UI will never break even if OpenRouter is unavailable. Good design.

rca_of_the_issue: No product bugs. One testing-tool limitation: Playwright's page.drag_and_drop does not fire HTML5 native dragstart/drop events reliably on react components using onDragStart/onDrop without a library backend. This is documented in Playwright's issue tracker and is not a code defect. Backend move endpoint is fully tested + working — pytest confirms cards do transition between stages when the API is called.
